([[Wolfeboro, New Hampshire]]) | college = {{ubl|[[Oregon Ducks men's basketball|Oregon]] (2018–2019)|[[City College of San Francisco|CC of San Francisco]] (2019–2020)|[[UC Santa Barbara Gauchos men's basketball|UC Santa Barbara]] (2020–2023)}} | draft_year = 2023 | career_start = 2023 | years1 = [[2023–24 NBA G League season|2023–2024]] | team1 = [[College Park Skyhawks]] | years2 = 2024 | team2 = [[Çağdaş Bodrumspor]] | years3 = [[2024–25 NBA G League season|2024–2025]] | team3 = [[Memphis Hustle]] | years4 = {{nbay|2024|end}} | team4 = [[Boston Celtics]] | years5 = [[2024–25 NBA G League season|2025]] | team5 = →[[Maine Celtics]] | years6 = 2025–2026 | team6 = [[FC Barcelona Bàsquet|FC Barcelona]] | years7 = 2026–present | team7 = [[FC Bayern Munich (basketball)|Bayern Munich]] | highlights = * Second-team All-[[Big West Conference|Big West]] (2023) }} ''' Miles Benjamin Norris''' (born April 15, 2000) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for [[FC Bayern Munich (basketball)|Bayern Munich]] of the [[Basketball Bundesliga]] (BBL) and the [[EuroLeague]]. He played [[college basketball]] for [[Oregon Ducks men's basketball|Oregon]], [[City College of San Francisco|CC of San Francisco]], and [[UC Santa Barbara Gauchos men's basketball|UC Santa Barbara]]. ==Early life and high school career== Norris grew up in [[San Diego]] and attended [[Mater Dei Catholic High School (Chula Vista, California)|Mater Dei Catholic High School]] in [[Chula Vista, California|Chula Vista]] for his freshman and sophomore years. Following his sophomore campaign, Norris was named All-CIF San Diego Section First Team after leading Mater Dei to a league title and CIF semifinals. For his junior season Norris attended [[Helix High School]] in [[La Mesa, California|La Mesa]] in which he averaged 11 points and 10 rebounds per game, helping Helix to a 31-win season and to the Division IV CIF State Championship Tournament game. Norris transferred to [[Brewster Academy]] in [[New Hampshire]] for his senior year where he helped Brewster claim the 2018 New England Prep School Athletic Council (NEPSAC) Class AAA regular season championship. He was rated a four-star recruit with a scout grade of 87 by ESPN and he was ranked 78th in ESPN's top-100 going into college.{{cite web|url=https://www.ucsbgauchos.com/sports/m-baskbl/2020-21/bios/Norris-Miles|title=Miles Norris|website=ucsbgauchos.com|access-date=July 6, 2023|date=July 6, 2023}} ==College career== Norris started his college career during the [[2018–19 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2018-19 season]] at the [[University of Oregon]], and appeared in 27 games all coming off the bench, averaging 10.5 minutes played per contest, 3.3 points and 1.9 rebounds per game.{{cite web|url=https://goducks.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/miles-norris/8109|title=Miles Norris|website=goducks.com|access-date=July 6, 2023|date=July 6, 2023}} He transferred to [[City College of San Francisco]] for his sophomore season. He helped CCSF to a 30–0 record, a Coast Conference north title and the Northern California Community College championship in 2019–20, where he averaged a team-leading 16.0 points, 6.1 rebounds, 1.4 blocked shots and 2.0 steals per game for the Rams.{{cite web|url=https://ccsfathletics.com/sports/mbkb/2019-20/bios/norris_miles_xkyp?view=bio|title=Miles Norris|website=ccsfathletics.com|access-date=July 6, 2023|date=July 6, 2023}} The following season Norris transferred again to [[UC Santa Barbara Gauchos men's basketball|UC Santa Barbara]] where he played three seasons from 2020 to 2023 averaging 29.8 minutes played, 11.6 points and 5.5 rebounds per game.{{cite web|url=https://www.ucsbgauchos.com/sports/m-baskbl/2020-21/bios/Norris-Miles|title=Miles Norris|website=ucsbgauchos.com|access-date=July 6, 2023|date=July 6, 2023}} ==Professional career== ===College Park Skyhawks (2023–2024)=== After going undrafted in the [[2023 NBA draft]], on July 6, 2023, Norris signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Atlanta Hawks]], splitting time with their [[NBA G League]] affiliate, [[College Park Skyhawks]].{{cite web|title=Atlanta Hawks Sign Forward Miles Norris to Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/news/atlanta-hawks-sign-forward-miles-norris-to-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|date=July 6, 2023|access-date=July 6, 2023}} On December 22, he was waived by Atlanta without playing for them{{cite tweet|author=Atlanta Hawks|title=We have requested waivers on two-way forward Miles Norris|number=1738240622631195076|user=ATLHawks|date=December 22, 2023|access-date=January 1, 2024}} and four days later, he was acquired by College Park.{{cite tweet|author=Skyhawks PR|title=The College Park Skyhawks have requested waivers on Malcom Rhett and have Celtics (2025)=== On March 2, 2025, Norris signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Boston Celtics]].{{cite web|title=Celtics signing forward Miles Norris to two-way deal|url=https://www.nbcsportsboston.com/nba/boston-celtics/miles-norris-contract-stats-highlights/691508/|website=nbcsportsboston.com|date=March 2, 2025|access-date=March 2, 2025}} In three appearances for the Celtics, he averaged 2.3 points and 3.0 rebounds. On August 10, Norris was waived by Boston.{{cite web | last=Terada | first=Souichi | title=Boston Celtics waive lengthy two-way forward, opening up spot | website=masslive | date=2025-08-10 |
